title: Finite direct image reflects bounded constructibility
statement:
Let $p:Z\to S$ be a
finite morphism of
Noetherian schemes and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring.
On ordinary derived
categories of etale modules, its
derived direct image $Rp_*$
reflects membership in
$D^b_c$.

proof.text: Let $K$ be any object of $D(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and represent it by a complex $C$. Finite direct image is exact on abelian sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. It is also exact on sheaves of modules over the same constant ring $\Lambda$: direct image has the same underlying abelian sheaf, and kernels and sheafified cokernels of module maps are those of the underlying abelian maps with their induced actions, as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to this exact module functor. Thus $Rp_*K$ is represented by the termwise complex $p_*C$ even when $K$ is not bounded below. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], for every integer $q$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)\cong p_*\mathcal H^q(K)$. This avoids assuming that $K$ is bounded below before that has been proved.

proof.text: First consider an etale sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules with $p_*G=0$. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] to its underlying abelian sheaf. For any geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, let $\bar s=p\bar z$ (using the same algebraically closed field), so the factor $G_{\bar z}$ occurs in the product $(p_*G)_{\bar s}\cong\prod_{\bar w\mid\bar s}G_{\bar w}$. If that product is zero, each factor is zero: put a proposed element of one factor in its coordinate and zero in the other coordinates. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to G$ on underlying abelian sheaves. This morphism is an isomorphism at every geometric stalk, hence $G=0$ as an abelian sheaf, and therefore also as a module sheaf. Now suppose $Rp_*K\in D^b_c(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and choose integers $a\le b$ outside which its cohomology is zero, using [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For every $q\notin[a,b]$, Step 1 gives $p_*\mathcal H^q(K)=0$, so the argument just given proves $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$. The same finite interval bounds $K$.

For each $q\in[a,b]$, the definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] says that $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*K)$ is constructible. Step 1 identifies this module sheaf with $p_*\mathcal H^q(K)$. Apply [lem-fin-finite-reflects-constructibility] to $\mathcal H^q(K)$: its hypotheses are precisely that $p$ is finite between Noetherian schemes, $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring, and $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is an etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules. Hence $\mathcal H^q(K)$ is constructible. Outside $[a,b]$ it is the zero sheaf, which is the constant sheaf with value the finite zero module, hence finite locally constant. For nonempty $Z$ the single stratum $Z$ proves constructibility; for empty $Z$ use the empty partition. These degreewise assertions and Step 2 give $K\in D^b_c(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$ by the same definition.
